blocks.text: Simplex Castings Limited (SCL) is a Chhattisgarh-based heavy engineering jobbing manufacturer. It melts and casts grey cast iron, alloy cast iron, SG iron and steel, and then fabricates, machines, assembles and tests the resulting components into equipment for capital-goods buyers. [F] (SCREENER) The company describes itself as a one-stop shop covering castings, fabrication, forging, machining, assembly, equipment building, in-house testing, an EPC division and a design wing. [F] (AR2025 p.45) It is not a mass-production foundry: management repeatedly stresses that the machine shop and foundry are deliberately flexible, working from a few kilos to 50-55 tonnes single-piece, because typical order quantities are one-off to five-off. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

Revenue is earned almost entirely from **contract manufacturing against customer drawings and tenders** - castings and fabricated assemblies sold to steel-plant OEMs, power-equipment OEMs, non-ferrous metal producers, pump/valve/gearbox/machine-tool makers, shipyards and ordnance factories. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) Management describes the business plainly: 'we are into contractual manufacturing' and 'we need to go up the value chain, which is a constant pressure on us'. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)

[F] (AR2025 p.41) There is no disclosed Unit-II: the third (Urla) unit, which was railway-dedicated, was sold to Texmaco in 2019. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) Group headcount is disclosed three different ways - 287 permanent employees on the rolls at 31 March 2025 [F] (AR2025 p.23), '1000+ total number of employees' [MC] (PPT Aug 2026) and 'about 1200 workers working' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) - the gap is presumably contract labour, but the documents never say so. Evidence-base warning that governs this entire report: our statements data set contains full-year statements only to March 2021 and quarterly data only to September 2021, with a trailing-twelve-month column ending in that quarter. [F] (NUMBERS) Everything from FY22 to Q1 FY27 - the entire period in which the business turned around - is available only from the annual report's five-year summary, a credit-rating press release and company presentations and calls. [F] (AR2025 p.5), [F] (RATING), [F] (PPT Aug 2026) No FY26 audited annual report and no quarterly filings after FY25 were available to us.

subsections.title: Listing status and what it means for the evidence base

blocks.text: SCL is not a recent listing. The company was listed in 1992 [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) and its equity trades on BSE under scrip code 513472 and symbol SIMPLEXCAS. [F] (AR2025 p.40) It is also nominally listed on the Calcutta Stock Exchange (scrip 29066); the board approved delisting from CSE in November 2022 and filed the application, but CSE suspended the company with effect from 5 April 2023 and the delisting has not been shown as completed. [F] (AR2025 p.20)

items: There is no prospectus or offer document in this dossier, because there has been no recent public issue; the capital raises have been preferential allotments. [F] (AR2025 p.20), [F] (CALL Feb 2026)

Consequence: there is no independently verified 'objects of the issue', no third-party-vetted capacity, order-book or customer disclosure, and no restated financial information of the kind an IPO would force. Every operating number after FY25 reaches the investor through management's own presentation or through a rating agency relying on company-supplied data. [AI]

The company registers itself as an MSME (Udyam-CG-05-0000018) on its own letterhead while simultaneously carrying overdue payables to micro and small enterprises, on which it has provided Rs 195.65 lakh of MSMED interest and paid none. [F] (PPT Aug 2026), [F] (AR2025 p.50), [F] (AR2025 p.95)

The registered office is being shifted from Maharashtra to Chhattisgarh; the first attempt (shareholder approval May 2023) failed on an MCA form error and the approval was re-sought at the 2025 AGM. The CIN on 2026 filings (L27320CT1980PLC019535) already differs from the CIN in the FY25 annual report (L27320MH1980PLC067459). [F] (AR2025 p.14), [F] (AR2025 p.42), [F] (PPT Aug 2026)

subsections.title: Bear thesis: the strongest reasons not to own it

items: 1. Four of the company's five credit rating agencies stopped rating it for non-cooperation in 2026, and the upgrade comes from the fifth. CRISIL moved the rating to 'issuer not cooperating' on 4 August 2026; ACUITE on 23 June 2026; India Ratings on 17 July 2026; Brickworks on 5 June 2026 - all for non-submission of information. Infomerics upgraded to IVR BBB/Stable on 10 September 2026. [F] (RATING) A company that has just re-rated its equity and is about to raise more capital does not benefit from four simultaneous non-cooperation notices, and management has not been asked about them on any call in this dossier. [AI]

2. The valuation inputs available to us are stale to the point of being unusable, and the market is being asked to pay a premium on numbers nobody can see. Our statements data show trailing twelve-month sales of Rs 90.91 cr and PAT of Rs 6.72 cr - figures that end in September 2021 - against a market capitalisation of Rs 517 cr and a share price of Rs 126, and produce a trailing P/E of 76.9x, EV/EBITDA of 30.1x and P/B of 8.46x. [F] (NUMBERS) The rating agency reports FY26 PAT of Rs 21.26 cr on the same company. [F] (RATING) These multiples are therefore hybrids of a current price and March-2021 fundamentals and we do not restate them.

3. Working capital is the historical failure mode and it has not yet been fixed. The rating agency puts the operating cycle at 150-200 days with receivables of 60-120 days and longer for government customers, and average working-capital utilisation at about 78% over the twelve months to June 2026. [F] (RATING) In FY25, trade receivables grew 107% (Rs 24.65 cr to Rs 51.14 cr) on 41% revenue growth. [F] (AR2025 p.61) The company already lost a Rs 110-130 cr revenue unit in 2019 because sanctioned working-capital limits were not disbursed. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)

4. The FY25 accounts contain revenue-recognition and vendor-charge items a sceptic should not ignore. The auditor flagged that Rs 1,097.19 lakh of revenue was derecognised at year-end because control had not transferred, now sitting as a liability (prior year: Rs 109.97 lakh netted off receivables) [F] (AR2025 p.51), [F] (AR2025 p.82); and Rs 152.84 lakh of liquidated-damage charges were netted off purchases on the basis of management's interpretation of contract terms. [F] (AR2025 p.50)

5. Profit is not yet cash. FY25 cash flow from operations was Rs 9.14 cr against PAT of Rs 15.13 cr, a CFO/PAT of 0.60x [E] (AR2025 p.63); the prior year CFO was negative Rs 2.96 cr. In our statements data, cumulative free cash flow over the three years to FY21 was negative Rs 44.2 cr. [F] (NUMBERS) No FY26 cash flow statement was available to us; the rating agency states only that FY26 CFO 'remained positive'. [F] (RATING)

6. The FY28 Rs 500 cr target explicitly depends on things that do not exist yet. Management states the Rs 500 cr number rests on acquisitions and EPC, then says capacity at the two existing units supports only 'Rs 300-350 cr', that the first acquisition attempt failed on valuation, that two others are open, and that the search has moved outside India for cheaper multiples. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026), [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) Separately, management says the EPC revenue is not in the Rs 500 cr target. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) Those statements are not mutually consistent. [AI]

7. Dilution is continuous and another round is already scheduled. Promoter holding has fallen from 56.53% (Sep 2023) to 50.36% (Jun 2026); preferential issues were made in FY25 (10,67,081 shares at Rs 75) and FY26 (Rs 50.15 cr). [F] (NUMBERS), [F] (AR2025 p.56), [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) A board meeting was called for 23 September 2026 to consider raising funds through equity or convertible securities - nine days after management said on the Q1 call that no further fundraise would be required. [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS), [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

8. Contingent liabilities are large relative to the pre-raise equity base. An income-tax demand of Rs 18.57 cr for AY 2018-19 is under appeal at CIT(A) Mumbai, against FY25 net worth of Rs 56.66 cr; counter-guarantees to banks stand at Rs 15.66 cr; an EPF demand of Rs 6.50 cr is at the Industrial Tribunal; a CENVAT appeal was rejected in January 2025 with a final hearing set for 29 July 2025 and no outcome disclosed. [F] (AR2025 p.85), [F] (AR2025 p.5)

9. Governance hygiene is weak in ways that recur. BSE fines in three consecutive years: Rs 11,800 (FY23, late board-meeting intimation), Rs 96,760 (FY24, audit-committee constitution, paid under protest), Rs 3.80 lakh plus GST (FY25, failure to apply for listing of allotted shares within 20 days). [F] (AR2025 p.36), [F] (AR2025 p.25) The independent director who chairs the audit, NRC, stakeholder and CSR committees is a partner of two firms that render professional services to the company. [F] (AR2025 p.33) The company secretary appears to have changed at least twice in about a year. [F] (AR2025 p.4), [F] (PPT Aug 2026), [F] (CALL Aug 2026)

10. Everything in the growth story is tender or order-dependent in a business with liquidated-damage exposure. Management deliberately caps the order book at Rs 100-150 cr because 'every order has liquidated damages... most are limited to 5%, but some go up to 10%'. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) The FY25 accounts carry Rs 109.73 lakh of liquidated damages as an expense (FY24: Rs 136.86 lakh) - this is a live, recurring cost, not a theoretical risk. [F] (AR2025 p.84)

rows: Is the margin step-up (10-11% to 18-19% EBITDA) structural?
Mix shift to complex, credential-gated items plus operating leverage and better material efficiency - the rating agency accepts this explanation [F] (RATING)

FY25 other expenses fell from Rs 32.13 cr to Rs 18.39 cr, driven by off-loading/job-contract charges (Rs 13.05 cr to Rs 5.29 cr) and sundry balances written off (Rs 4.91 cr to Rs 1.09 cr); raw material cost simultaneously rose from 54% to 67% of revenue [F] (AR2025 p.62), [F] (AR2025 p.84). Is the order book revenue visibility or a rolling quotation pipeline?
It has tripled off the historical Rs 80-100 cr base and now includes BHEL, ThyssenKrupp, SMS and Mazgaon Dock names [MC] (CALL Jun 2026), [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)

Management says it is deliberately kept at Rs 100-150 cr and 'we are trying to keep the order book to same level' - which means the order book is a capped work-in-hand measure, not a backlog that can grow into the Rs 300 cr guidance [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). No order-book ageing, execution schedule or book-to-bill is ever disclosed [F] (PPT Aug 2026)
A disclosed opening/closing order-book bridge with orders received, executed and cancelled
Does RDSO approval convert into railway revenue in FY27?
Approval is granted, capex is done, capacity is 200-250 sets/month, and payment cycles in railways are 15-30 days, which would also fix working capital [MC] (CALL Jun 2026), [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)

As of the August 2026 call the company was 'currently not doing any railway business'; bogie volumes wait on wagon orders being placed on wagon builders, which management has been expecting 'next month' since May 2026 [MC] (CALL Aug 2026), [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)
A disclosed first casted-bogie order with quantity and value, and monthly despatch numbers
Is the balance-sheet repair permanent or a function of repeated equity issues?
Gearing 0.47x and interest cover 5.48x at Mar-26 are comfortable and the company now uses non-debt receivable financing [F] (RATING), [F] (PPT Aug 2026)

The repair was funded by preferential equity, not by cash generation; working capital utilisation is still ~78%; unsecured related-party loans of Rs 26.11 cr were part of the FY25 funding mix; and another raise is already on the board agenda [F] (RATING), [F] (AR2025 p.80), [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS)
Two consecutive years of CFO exceeding PAT without a fresh equity round
Is defence/shipbuilding a real vertical or an optionality label?

ABS and IRS certifications, live A-bracket/B-bracket/stern-boss castings for Mazgaon Dock (5 sets, about Rs 4.5 cr, plus Rs 8 cr in pipeline), and components for Dhanush at Gun Carriage Factory Jabalpur [MC] (CALL Aug 2026), [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

Management caps the combined defence-plus-shipbuilding ambition at 10-15% of revenue and says Dhanush revenue is 'very low at the moment', maybe Rs 10-15 cr in a couple of years; the T-72 turret programme is dead ('turret is gone, sir') [MC] (CALL Feb 2026), [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)
Order announcements with values; whether the second Mazgaon order converts

blocks.text: The consensus framing available in this dossier - a Rs 200 cr foundry with an RDSO approval, a re-rated balance sheet and a Rs 500 cr FY28 aspiration - is directionally supported by the evidence, and the operating recovery from a loss-making FY20 to a Rs 21 cr PAT FY26 is real and verified by a third party. [F] (RATING) Our variant perception is about what kind of asset this is. The documents describe a **credential-gated jobbing shop** whose economics are set by tender selection, execution discipline and cash conversion, not a product company with recurring revenue - management itself says the company is moving 'from a jobbing to a product line, maybe for 50% of the topline' only prospectively and only if railways scales. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) On that reading, the two variables that actually matter are (i) whether the operating cycle falls from 150-200 days towards the 60-70 days management targets [F] (RATING), [MC] (CALL Aug 2026), and (ii) whether the company can grow without a further equity round - and the 23 September 2026 board meeting on fund-raising suggests the answer to the second is not yet yes. [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS) The market appears to be capitalising the growth narrative while the disclosure base needed to test it - audited FY26 statements, segment data, customer concentration, order-book bridge, export split - does not exist in any document available to us, and four rating agencies have just said the company is not submitting information to them. [F] (RATING), [AI]

subsections.title: What the timeline reveals about how recent the current business really is

items: The corporate shell is old; the current earnings profile is two years old. On the company's own five-year summary, PAT was Rs 1.01 cr (FY21), Rs 1.52 cr (FY22), negative Rs 16.99 cr (FY23), Rs 2.39 cr (FY24) and then Rs 15.13 cr (FY25). [F] (AR2025 p.5) Management's own words: 'last year was the first year. This is the second year where we are doing better.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

The revenue base is still below the pre-2019 level on a like-for-like footing. Management says FY19 revenue was Rs 220-230 cr including the Urla railway unit [MC] (CALL Feb 2026); our data show FY19 sales of Rs 137.28 cr on a consolidated basis [F] (NUMBERS) - the two are not reconciled - and FY26 revenue was Rs 202.90 cr. [F] (RATING)

The railway vertical being sold as new is a restoration, not an invention: the company made bogies until 2019 for 20-30 years and has supplied 12,000+ railway bogies historically. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026), [MC] (PPT Aug 2026) That cuts both ways - the capability is proven, but so is the fact that the company lost it once through a financing failure. [AI]

The EPC division that appears in the 'one-stop shop' description was disbanded in 2020 and the last order was executed in 2016; management is now 'exploring' EPC again. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) Investors reading the standing corporate description in the annual report and profile are reading a capability set that is partly dormant. [AI] (AR2025 p.45), [F] (SCREENER)

Simplex 2.0 is management's own label for a reset that began around FY25, with 'Simplex 3.0' floated as a later, more global phase after 'two, two and a half years'. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026), [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) The investment case is therefore being underwritten on roughly eight quarters of improved trading. [AI]

subsections.title: The production chain, step by step

items: 1. Qualification. Most PSU and OEM work is credential-gated: 'credentials are very important in our kind of industry... most of the things would have a prerequisite that what are your credentials for it'. Government buyers increasingly tender on the GeM portal. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) Formal qualifications named: RDSO (wagon, mechanical), American Bureau of Shipping and Indian Bureau of Shipping. [F] (PPT Aug 2026), [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

2. Bidding and order selection. Orders come as tenders or negotiated OEM packages. Management explicitly selects for load to its own shops - for EPC it will 'quote only for the packages which give us at least 30-40% load to our factories'. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

3. Design and pattern. The company has a design wing; for Russian-design steel plants the drawings come from the customer. [F] (AR2025 p.45), [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) For coke-oven doors the design is the company's own, evolved from the 1987 Japanese collaboration - the one place where design value is captured. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)

4. Melting and casting. Foundry with electric arc furnaces; the fifth EAF was being commissioned as at the FY25 annual report and the rating agency still describes EAF commissioning as in process in September 2026. [F] (AR2025 p.3), [F] (RATING) Rating agency describes the work-in-process chain as pattern and structure preparation, mould making, melting, pouring, cooling, fettling, heat treatment and inspection. [F] (RATING)
5. Fabrication. Separate heavy engineering and fabrication shop, capacity stated at 15,000+ MTPA. [F] (PPT Aug 2026)

6. Machining. Central machine shop with a large number of CNCs; management states more than 100 machine tools, but no 5-axis or higher machines ('we don't have at the moment because it was not required for our kind of products'). [F] (AR2025 p.45), [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

7. Assembly, testing and despatch. In-house testing; for bogies the company buys springs, side bearers, brakes and elastomeric pads from outside and assembles the complete set. [F] (AR2025 p.45), [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

8. Inspection and acceptance. Customers - particularly OEMs, railways and infrastructure entities - require inspection and approval before acceptance, so finished goods sit in inventory until cleared. [F] (RATING) This is the mechanism that produced FY25 finished-goods inventory of Rs 23.40 cr (up from Rs 10.42 cr) and the Rs 10.97 cr revenue derecognition. [F] (AR2025 p.78), [F] (AR2025 p.51)

9. Collection. Receivables of 60-120 days, longer for government and large institutional customers; now partly accelerated by TReDS bill discounting at 5-5.5% annualised. [F] (RATING), [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

subsections.title: Where value is captured, and where it is not

blocks.text: Value is captured at exactly three points on the disclosed evidence. First, **design-owning products**: coke-oven doors carry 'an element of design involved, and there is some guarantees involved... there are fewer players, because Simplex is one of those kind of monopolistic players there, so I get better margins'. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) Second, **credential-gated tenders** where the bidder list is short. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) Third, **integration**: the ability to deliver a machined, assembled package rather than a raw casting - 'each and every level that we add, we become less of a foundry, more of a solution to the customer'. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)

Value is explicitly not captured in the two largest growth vectors. Management is unusually candid that railways and power-sector fabrication 'will be at similar margins to what we have at the moment... they are all tender business. It will be similar to what we have been able to do' and that in fabrication and railways 'PAT will not be higher. Definitely they will not be higher.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) The plan to raise blended margins therefore depends on being 'choosy' in the remaining, non-railway, non-power base - a mix argument, not a pricing-power argument. [AI]

The economic identity of this business is: **flexibility sold as a service**. Management's own explanation of why it wins in power, railways, steel, defence and shipbuilding is a single sentence - 'the range that we have, few kilos to 20, 30, 40, 50 tons, and all kinds of machines' - because those sectors need one-off to five-off heavy items that dedicated-line foundries cannot economically make. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) That is a real but capped advantage: it explains high mix flexibility and long work-in-process, which is precisely why the operating cycle runs 150-200 days. [F] (RATING), [AI]

items: Outsourcing is material and volatile. Off-loading / job contract charges were Rs 5.29 cr in FY25 against Rs 13.05 cr in FY24 - from 10.7% of revenue to 3.1%. [F] (AR2025 p.84), [E] Over the same year raw material and component consumption rose from 53.9% to 67.1% of revenue. [E] (AR2025 p.62) The pattern is consistent with bringing previously off-loaded work in-house, which flatters gross-margin-adjacent lines and is a key reason the reported EBITDA margin step is not purely price or mix. [AI]

Capital intensity is moderate by foundry standards but rising. Net block was Rs 33.83 cr at 31 March 2025 against revenue of Rs 171.88 cr - a fixed-asset turn above 5x - with capital work-in-progress of Rs 12.38 cr on top. [E] (AR2025 p.61) Our statements data show a fixed-asset turnover of 1.88x in FY21, when revenue was a third of today's. [F] (NUMBERS)

The incremental capex programme is small relative to the growth targeted: about Rs 15 cr spent in FY26 and Rs 25 cr planned for FY27, against a revenue step from Rs 203 cr to a targeted Rs 300 cr. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) Management claims an asset turn of 'at least 3-4x' on the Rs 25 cr. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)

The heavier capital need is working capital, not fixed capital. Half of the Rs 50.15 cr raise was earmarked for working capital, and management describes the equipment business as taking 6-8 months from order to payment. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026), [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Foundry expansion is being avoided: 'Foundry is more of debottlenecking... we are not wanting to put too much of capex at one point of time', with a machine-moulding plant explicitly 'not at the card, nothing at the moment, just on the drawing board stage'. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)
